title: Negotiating and persuading / Kɔkɔdɔm ne kɔkɔbɔ
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛkasa kɔkɔbɔ a, yɛnkyɛn yɛn ara yɛde asɛm bɛbɛ kama a wɔde 'sɛ wotwa' anaa 'wɔhwɛ' ne subjunctive wɔ clauses a wɔde 'sɛ'. Wɔ English, B2 kyerɛ sɛ wɔhwɛ kwan pa a wɔde 'would', 'could', 'might' ne 'I was wondering if...'. Hwehwɛ sɛ wode 'hacer una contraoferta' kyerɛ 'to make a counteroffer' (yiye) nanso verb 'to suggest' nni subjunctive wɔ English, na sɛ yɛde base form a verb no (suggest + infinitive). Enti, 'tag questions' a wɔde ma wabu akwantu no (isn't it?) nni sɛ '¿no?' efisɛ wɔ English no wɔhwɛ auxiliary verb a wɔde wɔ main clause no.
rule: Sɛ wubɛkasa kɔkɔdɔm ne kɔkɔbɔ wɔ English B2 a, wɔde: 1) Modal verbs ma asɛm no yɛn: 'would' (I would appreciate...), 'could' (Could we...), 'might' (That might work). 2) Politeness structures: 'I was wondering if...', 'Would it be possible to...?', 'If you could..., that would be...'. 3) Expressions ma wɔde ma wɔyɛ concessions: 'That's a fair point, but...', 'I see what you mean, however...'. 4) Phrases ma wɔde ma wɔtwa agreement: 'What if we...?', 'How about...? + -ing', 'Would you be open to...?'. 5) Conditional ma wɔde ma wɔbɔ hypothesis: 'If we lowered the price, would you buy two?' (second conditional). Sɛ kɔkɔbɔ a, wɔde phrases sɛ 'Think of it this way...', 'The way I see it...', 'It's worth considering that...'. Pa a, wɔ English no, 'suggest' ne 'recommend' de that + subject + verb wɔ base form (without 's'), anaa wɔde gerund: 'I suggest that we wait' / 'I suggest waiting'. Wɔnni subjunctive sɛ Twi.

concept_examples.text: Could we possibly meet halfway on the price?
concept_examples.translation: Ɛnyɛ yɛbɛtwa animuonyam wɔ price no so?
concept_examples.phonetic: /kʊd wi ˈpɒsəbli miːt ˌhæfˈweɪ ɒn ðə praɪs/

concept_examples.text: I was wondering if you might consider a discount for bulk orders.
concept_examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ wuhwɛ sɛ wubɛma me discount ma me wholesale orders no.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɒz ˈwʌndərɪŋ ɪf ju maɪt kənˈsɪdər ə dɪskaʊnt fɔː bʌlk ˈɔːrdərz/

concept_examples.text: What if we extend the deadline by a week? That could work for both of us.
concept_examples.translation: Sɛ yɛbɔ time frame no paa a, ɛno ara na ɛbɛyɛ ma yɛn nyinaa?
concept_examples.phonetic: /wɒt ɪf wi ɪkˈstend ðə dedlaɪn baɪ ə wiːk ðæt kʊd wɜːrk fɔːr boʊθ əv ʌs/

concept_examples.text: If you agree to a lower price, we'll sign the contract today.
concept_examples.translation: Sɛ wotwa price a ɛho a, yɛbɛsign contract no today.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf ju əˈɡriː tʊ ə loʊər praɪs wiːl saɪn ðə ˈkɒntrækt təˈdeɪ/

common_error.wrong: I suggest that we should wait until next week.
common_error.correct: I suggest that we wait until next week.
common_error.correct_alt: I suggest waiting until next week.
common_error.explanation: Error no fi asɛm a wɔde wɔ Twi no ho a wɔde 'sugiero que debamos esperar' ne verb 'should'. Wɔ English no, after 'suggest' (ne 'recommend', 'propose'), wɔde English subjunctive, a ɛne base form a verb no (without 's' ne 'should'). Wɔde gerund structure as alternative. Pa a, ɛsɛ sɛ wubuu sɛ Twi subjunctive no nni sɛ wɔde wɔ English no; wɔde base form ma wɔde nyinaa subjects, even 'he/she/it'.

levels.label: Softening requests and proposals
levels.translation: Ma request ne proposal no yɛn

examples.original: Would it be possible to get an extension?
examples.phonetic: /wʊd ɪt bi ˈpɒsəbl tə ɡet ən ɪkˈstenʃən/
examples.translation: Ɛyɛ possible sɛ mebɛhya extension?
examples.note: Yɛde 'would' anaa 'will' ma asɛm no yɛn, sɛ 'Ɛyɛ possible?' wɔ Twi.

examples.original: I was wondering if you could lower the price.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɒz ˈwʌndərɪŋ ɪf ju kʊd ˈloʊər ðə praɪs/
examples.translation: Mepɛ sɛ wuhwɛ sɛ wubɛyɛ price no ho.
examples.note: 'I was wondering if...' structure no yɛ common paa wɔ negotiations. Nnyɛ 'I wondered' a ɛyɛ direct.

examples.original: Could we possibly agree on a different payment schedule?
examples.phonetic: /kʊd wi ˈpɒsəbli əˈɡriː ɒn ə ˈdɪfrənt ˈpeɪmənt ˈʃedjuːl/
examples.translation: Ɛyɛ possible sɛ yɛbɛtwa payment schedule biara?
examples.note: 'Possibly' ma asɛm no yɛn paa. Wɔ Twi no, yɛde 'Ɛyɛ possible?', nanso 'possibly' de after subject.

levels.label: Making counteroffers and concessions
levels.translation: Ma wɔyɛ counteroffers ne concessions

examples.original: That's a fair point, but we can't go below ten percent.
examples.phonetic: /ðæts ə feər pɔɪnt bʌt wi kænt ɡəʊ bɪˈloʊ ten pəˈsent/
examples.translation: ɛyɛ point paa, nanso yɛnntɔ ten percent.
examples.note: Sɛ wotwa obi point no a (That's a fair point) ɛne paa before woyii.

examples.original: If you agree to a longer contract, we could offer a better rate.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf ju əˈɡriː tʊ ə ˈlɒŋɡər ˈkɒntrækt wi kʊd ˈɒfər ə ˈbetər reɪt/
examples.translation: Sɛ wotwa contract a ɛho a, yɛbɛma mo better rate.
examples.note: Second conditional (if + past, would/could) de ma wɔde ma wɔbɔ hypothetical conditions.

examples.original: How about reducing the quantity instead of the price?
examples.phonetic: /haʊ əˈbaʊt rɪˈdjuːsɪŋ ðə ˈkwɒntəti ɪnˈsted əv ðə praɪs/
examples.translation: Ԑdeɛn na quantity no ho anaa price no?
examples.note: 'How about + -ing' yɛ natural way ma wɔde ma wɔsuggest alternatives.

levels.label: Persuading and reaching agreement
levels.translation: Ma wɔkɔkɔbɔ ne ma wɔtwa agreement

examples.original: Think of it this way: a lower upfront cost saves you money in the long run.
examples.phonetic: /θɪŋk əv ɪt ðɪs weɪ ə loʊər ʌpˈfrʌnt kɒst seɪvz ju ˈmʌni ɪn ðə lɒŋ rʌn/
examples.translation: Hwɛ no sɛe: initial cost a ɛho no ma woyɛ savings wɔ long term.
examples.note: 'Think of it this way' yɛ useful expression ma wɔde ma wɔreframe perspective.

examples.original: Would you be open to a trial period for three months?
examples.phonetic: /wʊd ju bi ˈoʊpən tʊ ə ˈtraɪəl ˈpɪəriəd fɔː θriː mʌnθs/
examples.translation: Ԑdeɛn na wɔbɛyɛ ma wɔde three months trial period?
examples.note: 'Open to' yɛ verbal phrase a ɛnni direct equivalent wɔ Twi; ɛma wɔde sɛ 'disposed to consider'.

examples.original: If we meet your deadline, will you extend the payment terms?
examples.phonetic: /ɪf wi miːt jɔːr dedlaɪn wɪl ju ɪkˈstend ðə ˈpeɪmənt tɜːmz/
examples.translation: Sɛ yɛbɔ deadline no a, wɔbɛyɛ ma wɔde payment terms no?
examples.note: First conditional (if + present, will) de ma wɔde ma wɔbɔ real conditions ne ma wɔde ma wɔnegotiate.

examples.original: I'm confident we can find a solution that works for both sides.
examples.phonetic: /aɪm ˈkɒnfɪdənt wi kæn faɪnd ə səˈluːʃən ðæt wɜːks fɔːr boʊθ saɪdz/
examples.translation: Mebɔ sɛ yɛbɛhua solution bi a ɛbɛyɛ ma yɛn nyinaa.
examples.note: Sɛ wode 'I'm confident' anaa 'I think' a, ɛma asɛm no yɛ strong ne ma wɔkɔkɔbɔ.

title: Giving and justifying opinions in depth / Kyɛfoɔ ne kyerɛwfoɔ ma wɔ akoma ntoso
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛnka ‘mɛyɛ ahu’ anaa ‘mɛyɛ adwene’ ne ‘efusɛ’ ma yɛkyerɛkyerɛ yɛn adwene. Wɔ English mu, sɛ wopɛ ma wokyɛfoɔ ne wɔkyerɛwfoɔ ntoso a, ebia wo ho asɛm nkyerɛaseɛ ne mmoa no wɔ ‘the reason being’, ‘due to’, ‘given that’, ne mmoa a wɔde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ anaa ɛyɛeɛ a wɔtwa so ‘if... then...’. Fa so nhwɛ sɛdeɛ wode ‘according to my opinion’ (sɛnea ɛte saa ara na ɛnyɛ adwene) kyerɛ ‘in my opinion’.
rule: Ma wode akoma ntoso kyɛfoɔ ne kyerɛwfoɔ wɔ English mu no, hwɛ: 1) Kyɛfoɔ asɛm: ‘In my view’, ‘From my perspective’, ‘I would argue that’, ‘It seems to me that’. 2) Kyerɛwfoɔ: ‘The reason for this is’, ‘This is due to’, ‘Given that’, ‘Considering that’. 3) Kɔ so kyerɛwfoɔ: ‘However’, ‘On the other hand’, ‘While it is true that...’, ‘Nevertheless’. 4) Mmoa a wɔde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ: ‘If... then’, ‘Unless...’, ‘Provided that...’. 5) Sɛdeɛ ɛyɛeɛ a wɔtwa so: ‘This leads to’, ‘As a result’, ‘Consequently’. B2: Ebia wo ho asɛm nkyerɛaseɛ ne mmoa a wɔde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ no yɛ ntoso ne yɛ akoma mu.

concept_examples.text: In my view, remote work has increased productivity, the reason being that employees avoid long commutes.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛyɛ adwene sɛ, ɔmanfoɔ a wɔtɔn awerɛhow mu wɔ hyɛne mu no, wɔn werɛhyɛmu ayɛ. Efusɛ, wɔn a wɔhyɛ nea wɔbɛyɛ no, wɔnntɔn ntɛm.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪn maɪ vjuː, rɪˈmoʊt wɜːrk hæz ˈɪnkriːst ˌprɒdʌkˈtɪvəti, ðə ˈriːzn ˈbiːɪŋ ðæt ˌemploʊˈiːz əˈvɔɪd lɔːŋ kəˈmjuːts/

concept_examples.text: I would argue that investing in education yields long-term benefits, given that it improves social mobility.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛyɛ ahu sɛ, sɛ yɛbɔɔ adwuma wɔ akwantuomu no, ɛbɛma yɛn ahohia mpo a ɛfiri awerɛhow mu no ayɛ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wʊd ˈɑːrgjuː ðæt ɪnˈvestɪŋ ɪn ˌedʒuˈkeɪʃn jiːldz lɔːŋ tɜːrm ˈbenɪfɪts, ˈɡɪvn ðæt ɪt ɪmˈpruːvz ˈsoʊʃl moʊˈbɪləti/

concept_examples.text: From my perspective, the new policy is flawed, due to the fact that it ignores regional differences.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛyɛ adwene sɛ, sɛ yɛbɔɔ adwuma wɔ akwantuomu no, ɛbɛma yɛn ahohia mpo a ɛfiri awerɛhow mu no ayɛ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /frɒm maɪ pərˈspektɪv, ðə nuː ˈpɒləsi ɪz flɔːd, djuː tuː ðə fækt ðæt ɪt ɪɡˈnɔːrz ˈriːdʒənl ˈdɪfrənsɪz/

concept_examples.text: It seems to me that we should prioritize renewable energy, otherwise we will face severe climate consequences.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛyɛ ahu sɛ, sɛ yɛmmfa yɛn adwuma wɔ akwantuomu no, yɛbɛka awerɛhow a ɛyɛ den na ɛyɛ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪt siːmz tuː miː ðæt wiː ʃʊd praɪˈɒrɪtaɪz rɪˈnjuːəbl ˈenərdʒi, ˈʌðəwaɪz wiː wɪl feɪs sɪˈvɪər ˈklaɪmət ˈkɒnsɪkwənsɪz/

common_error.wrong: According to my opinion, the government should do more for education.
common_error.correct: In my opinion, the government should do more for education.
common_error.correct_alt: From my point of view, the government should do more for education.
common_error.explanation: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛka ‘mɛyɛ adwene sɛ’ (literally ‘according to my opinion’), nanso wɔ English mu no, ɛnyɛ adwene. ‘According to’ de ma wɔde kyerɛ kwan a wɔfi so hyia biara (according to the report). Sɛdeɛ ɛte saa ara na ɛyɛ ne ‘in my opinion’ anaa ‘from my point of view’. Nkɔsoɔ a ɛte saa ara na ɛyɛ no yɛ den wɔ Twi kasafoɔ mu efusɛ ‘according to’ a wɔde kyerɛ ‘according to’ no, wɔde ma no wɔ mmoa a wɔde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ mu.

levels.label: Introducing Opinions
levels.translation: Deɛ mɛyɛ adwene

examples.original: In my view, the film was overrated.
examples.phonetic: /ɪn maɪ vjuː, ðə fɪlm wɒz ˌoʊvərˈreɪtɪd/
examples.translation: Mɛyɛ adwene sɛ, ɔmanfoɔ a wɔtɔn awerɛhow mu wɔ hyɛne mu no, wɔn werɛhyɛmu ayɛ.
examples.note: Hwɛ ‘in my view’ ma wode kyɛfoɔ a ɛte saa ara na ɛyɛ. Ɛso na woka ‘to my mind’ (mɛyɛ adwene) nanso ɛte saa ara na ɛyɛ wɔ British English mu.

examples.original: I strongly believe that recycling should be mandatory.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˈstrɔːŋli bɪˈliːv ðæt rɪˈsaɪklɪŋ ʃʊd biː ˈmændətɔːri/
examples.translation: Mɛyɛ ahu sɛ, sɛ yɛbɔɔ adwuma wɔ akwantuomu no, ɛbɛma yɛn ahohia mpo a ɛfiri awerɛhow mu no ayɛ.
examples.note: ‘Strongly believe’ de ma wode kyɛfoɔ a ɛte saa ara na ɛyɛ; wɔ Twi mu yɛde ‘mɛyɛ ahu’.

examples.original: As far as I'm concerned, the project is on track.
examples.phonetic: /æz fɑːr æz aɪm kənˈsɜːrnd, ðə ˈprɒdʒekt ɪz ɒn træk/
examples.translation: Sɛdeɛ mɛhu no, adwuma no yɛ den.
examples.note: Sɛdeɛ ɛte saa ara na ɛyɛ no, ɛma wode kyɛfoɔ a ɛte saa ara na ɛyɛ.

levels.label: Justifying with Reasons
levels.translation: Kyerɛwfoɔ a wɔde ma

examples.original: The reason being that prices have risen significantly.
examples.phonetic: /ðə ˈriːzn ˈbiːɪŋ ðæt ˈpraɪsɪz hæv ˈrɪzən sɪɡˈnɪfɪkəntli/
examples.translation: Efusɛ, wɔn a wɔhyɛ nea wɔbɛyɛ no, wɔnntɔn ntɛm.
examples.note: Wɔde ma no akyerɛkyerɛ deɛ ɛfiri so akyi.

examples.original: Due to the lack of funding, the program was cancelled.
examples.phonetic: /djuː tuː ðə læk ɒv ˈfʌndɪŋ, ðə ˈproʊɡræm wɒz ˈkænsəld/
examples.translation: Efiri sɛ wɔn a wɔhyɛ nea wɔbɛyɛ no, wɔnntɔn ntɛm, na adwuma no ayi.
examples.note: ‘Due to’ yɛ ntoso kaa ‘because of’. Hwɛ ‘to’ na mmom ‘because’.

examples.original: Given that the economy is unstable, we should be cautious.
examples.phonetic: /ˈɡɪvn ðæt ði ɪˈkɒnəmi ɪz ʌnˈsteɪbl, wiː ʃʊd biː ˈkɔːʃəs/
examples.translation: Efiri sɛ ɔmanfoɔ no wɔ awerɛhow a ɛnyɛ den mu no, ɛsɛ sɛ yɛbɛyɛ den.
examples.note: ‘Given that’ de ma wɔde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ anaa ɛyɛeɛ a wɔhu.

levels.label: Nuanced Argumentation
levels.translation: Kyerɛwfoɔ a wɔde ntoso

examples.original: While it is true that technology has drawbacks, it also opens up new possibilities.
examples.phonetic: /waɪl ɪt ɪz truː ðæt tekˈnɒlədʒi hæz ˈdrɔːbæks, ɪt ˈɔːlsoʊ ˈoʊpənz ʌp nuː ˌpɒsəˈbɪlətiz/
examples.translation: Ɛhɔ na awerɛhow ne mmoa wɔ, nanso ɛma yɛn akoma ntoso.
examples.note: Sɛdeɛ ɛte saa ara na ɛyɛ no, ɛma wode kyɛfoɔ a ɛte saa ara na ɛyɛ.

examples.original: Unless we address climate change now, future generations will suffer.
examples.phonetic: /ənˈles wiː əˈdres ˈklaɪmət tʃeɪndʒ naʊ, ˈfjuːtʃər ˌdʒenəˈreɪʃnz wɪl ˈsʌfər/
examples.translation: Sɛ yɛmmfa yɛn adwuma wɔ akwantuomu no, yɛbɛka awerɛhow a ɛyɛ den na ɛyɛ.
examples.note: Hwɛ ‘unless’ sɛnea ɛte saa ara na ɛyɛ (mmoa a ɛnyɛ den).

examples.original: If the government invested more in healthcare, the overall well-being would improve.
examples.phonetic: /ɪf ðə ˈɡʌvənmənt ɪnˈvestɪd mɔːr ɪn ˈhelθkeər, ði ˌoʊvərˈɔːl ˌwelˈbiːɪŋ wʊd ɪmˈpruːv/
examples.translation: Sɛ ɔmanfoɔ no bɔɔ adwuma wɔ akwantuomu no, ɛbɛma wɔn ahohia mpo a ɛfiri awerɛhow mu no ayɛ.
examples.note: Mmoa a ɛnyɛ den a ɛde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ. Wɔ English mu, yɛde kyerɛwfoɔ a ɛte saa ara na ɛyɛ wɔ mmoa a ɛde kyerɛ sɛdeɛ ɛbɛyɛ mu.

translations.tw: Kyɛfoɔ ne kyerɛwfoɔ ma wɔ akoma ntoso

title: Hypothesising about the past / Kasa kyerɛw nea ɛsɛeɛ
bridge: Wɔ Twi, sɛ yɛbɛka kyerɛw nea ɛsɛeɛ no, yɛnka 'sɛ ɛbɛyɛ' anaa 'sɛ ɛbɛyɛe', nanso wɔ English no, ɛnyɛ ɛno ne ɛno: wɔka 'would have + past participle' ma nea ɛsɛeɛ no ho abuafoɔ ne 'had + past participle' ma nea ɛsɛeɛ no ho adwuma. Ɛyɛ den sɛ wɔbɛka 'si habría' kyerɛ 'if would have', nanso wɔ English no, ɛmmfaso sɛ wɔbɛka 'would' wɔ nea ɛsɛeɛ no ho adwuma mu. Anaa, wɔ English no, wɔka 'might have' ne 'could have' ma ɛho nhyehyɛe anaa ɛho adwene, na wɔ Twi no, ɛno biara yɛ 'ɛbɛka' anaa 'ɛbɛyɛ'.
rule: Sɛ yɛbɛka kyerɛw nea ɛsɛeɛ no wɔ English no, yɛnka 'third conditional' ne modal structures bi wɔ hɔ. Nea ɛsoɔ no yɛ: 'If + past perfect (had + participle), would have + past participle'. Kyerɛw: 'If I had studied, I would have passed'. Yɛnka modals bi wɔ hɔ: 'could have' (ability anaa nhyehyɛe), 'might have' (nhyehyɛe), 'should have' (kyerɛw anaa akwantu). Wɔ indirect speech anaa wɔ kyerɛw no mu, yɛnka 'wish + past perfect' (mea ɛsɛeɛ). Ɛmmfaso sɛ wɔbɛka 'would have' wɔ 'if' clause mu. Wɔ question mu, yɛbɛkyerɛkyerɛ subject no: 'Would you have...?'

concept_examples.text: If I had known, I would have told you.
concept_examples.translation: Sɛ mɛwusua a, mɛkae wo.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɪf aɪ hæd noʊn, aɪ wʊd hæv toʊld juː/

concept_examples.text: She might have missed the train.
concept_examples.translation: Ɔno ara nea ɛbɛka ɛno.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː maɪt hæv mɪst ðə treɪn/

concept_examples.text: We could have won the match.
concept_examples.translation: Yɛno nea yɛbɛka yɛno.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː kʊd hæv wʌn ðə mætʃ/

concept_examples.text: I wish I had studied more.
concept_examples.translation: Mɛda a, mɛtumi ayɛ.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɪʃ aɪ hæd ˈstʌdɪd mɔːr/

common_error.wrong: If I would have known, I would have told you.
common_error.correct: If I had known, I would have told you.
common_error.correct_alt: Had I known, I would have told you.
common_error.explanation: Ɛyɛ den sɛ wɔbɛka 'Sɛ mɛwusua a' na mmusuafoɔ bɛka 'would have', nanso wɔ English no, ɛmmfaso sɛ wɔbɛka 'would' wɔ nea ɛsɛeɛ no ho adwuma mu. Ɛsɛ sɛ wɔbɛka 'had + participle' wɔ nea ɛsɛeɛ no ho adwuma mu. Sɛ wopɛ sɛ woyɛ ɛno nkyea a, kyerɛkyerɛ subject no ne 'had': 'Had I known...'.

levels.label: Third Conditional
levels.translation: Third Conditional

title: Discussing abstract concepts / Kasa mu nsɛm pɛnkyerɛnee
bridge: Wɔ Twiriso, sɛ yɛbɛka nsɛm pɛnkyerɛnee ho asɛm, yɛnkyea adwene kɛ yɛbɔ mmara a ɛso wɔ ‘ɛsɛ sɛ...’, ‘mɛma adwene sɛ ɛyɛ...’ na sɛntɛn mma bu a wɔde bɔ mmara. Wɔ Gyenman ne Nsonaso, mmara a wɔde bɔ mu nsɛm pɛnkyerɛnee so ho asɛm biara rekɔ hyia sɛ wɔde ‘suggest’, ‘recommend’, ‘demand’, anaa nsɛm a wɔbɔ mmara wɔ ‘it is essential that...’. Enti, wɔ Gyenman ne Nsonaso, nsɛmpua a ɛte sɛ ‘freedom’ anaa ‘justice’ a wɔka ho asɛm pɛnkyerɛnee no, wɔntumi de bɔfoɔ maa no, na wɔ Twiriso no, wɔde bɔfoɔ ‘la’ maa no biara. Nso, hu sɛ wɔ Gyenman ne Nsonaso no, wɔde ‘do’ kyerɛkyerɛ sɛ wɔrebɛbu anaa wɔrenbu, na adjekit no nni abɔ a ɛso wɔ subject no so.
rule: Sɛ wubɛka nsɛm pɛnkyerɛnee ho asɛm wɔ Gyenman ne Nsonaso no, ɛsɛ sɛ wuhwe hwɛ: 1. Nsɛmpua pɛnkyerɛnee a ɛwɔ singular/plural a wɔde ‘zero article’ maa no sɛ woka ho asɛm pɛnkyerɛnee (‘Freedom is important’ vs ‘La libertad es importante’). 2. Sɛntɛn a wɔbɔ mmara wɔ ‘that’ + verb wɔ base form (subjuntivo) a ɛho hia wɔ verb a ɛte sɛ recommendation anaa demand (‘I suggest that she be...’) na wɔ some adjectives (‘It is crucial that he attend’). 3. Sɛntɛn a wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ adwene: ‘In my opinion’, ‘I believe that’, ‘It seems to me that’, a wɔde indicative maa no (sɛ wɔ Twiriso no, wɔde subjuntivo maa no). 4. Sɛntɛn a wɔde ‘which’ na ‘that’ maa no sɛ wubɛkyerɛkyerɛ anaa wunnyi ho kwan. 5. Modal verbs a wɔde kyerɛkyerɛ: ‘might’, ‘could’, ‘would’, ‘should’ sɛ wubɛka ho asɛm a ɛte sɛ possibility, condition anaa advice. 6. Sɛntɛn a wɔde ‘it’ maa no (‘It is obvious that’, ‘It is worth considering’). Hwe hwɛ sɛ wɔ Gyenman ne Nsonaso no, wɔnni double negation, na sɛntɛn no ho nhyehyɛe no yɛ Subject + Verb + Object.

title: Expressing complex emotions / Kyerεw Kronkron Adwenee
bridge: Wɔ Twi mu, yɛnkyerɛ yɛde asɛm a ɛso edwuma pa a wɔde kyerε adwenee, sɛ ‘wɔyɛ’ anaa ‘wɔte’ ne dwuma a wɔde kyerε adwenee, noko wɔ Gyenman mu, wɔde nkyerɛkyerɛ a wɔwɔ ho kyɛn kyɛn, sɛdeɛ wɔde kyerɛ adwenee a wɔwɔ ho kyɛn kyɛn, sɛdeɛ wɔde kyerɛ adwenee a wɔwɔ ho kyɛn kyɛn, sɛdeɛ wɔde kyerɛ adwenee a wɔwɔ ho kyɛn kyɛn. Ɛyɛ den sɛ wɔde ‘tengo miedo de’ kyerε ‘I have fear of’ na ɛnnyɛ ‘I'm afraid of’. Enti, Gyenman kyerεw adwenee a wɔwɔ ho kyɛn kyɛn sɛdeɛ Twi nni asɛm biara a ɛde kyerε, sɛ ‘frustrated’ (frustrado) ne ‘annoyed’ (molesto), anaa ‘overwhelmed’ (abrumado) a ɛnni aka ho asɛm biara. Fa akoma yɛ adwenee ne dwuma a wɔde kyerɛ adwenee a wɔwɔ ho kyɛn kyɛn.
rule: Ma wɔde kyerɛ adwenee a wɔwɔ ho kyɛn kyɛn wɔ Gyenman mu, wɔde: 1) Adjetivos ne preposiciones a wɔwɔ ho kyɛn kyɛn: 'angry about/at', 'frustrated with', 'disappointed in/with', 'excited about', 'worried about', 'ashamed of', 'proud of'. 2) Nkyerɛkyerɛ a wɔde 'feel' + adjetivo anaa 'feel like' + gerundio ma wɔde kyerɛ adwenee a wɔwɔ ho kyɛn kyɛn. 3) Dwuma a wɔde 'get' + adjetivo ma wɔde kyerɛ adwenee a wɔwɔ ho kyɛn kyɛn (get frustrated, get overwhelmed). 4) Adjetivos a wɔwɔ ho kyɛn kyɛn ne mmoa a wɔde kyerɛ adwenee a wɔwɔ ho kyɛn kyɛn: 'homesick', 'heartbroken', 'overwhelmed'. 5) Mmoa a wɔde kyerɛ adwenee a wɔwɔ ho kyɛn kyɛn: 'on cloud nine' (sɛ wɔyɛ paa), 'down in the dumps' (sɛ wɔyɛ mframa). Fa akoma sɛ 'nervous' de kyerε anxiety, 'anxious' de kyerε worry a ɛso edwuma pa; 'upset' so edwuma pa kɛkɛ 'sad'. Mmom ‘I have’ ne adwenee nni Gyenman mu, gye mmoa sɛ ‘I have a feeling’.

title: Formal Writing: Reports and Emails / Nkontompo a wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara
bridge: Wɔ Twi, nkontompo a wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara so tumi ayɛ ahyɛ a wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara a wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara. Wɔ English, wɔde akyirekyerɛ ne ahyɛ a wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara. Adwuma a wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara bi ne sɛ wɔde 'Le adjunto' kyerɛw 'I attach' (mmara) na ɛnne 'Please find attached' anaa 'I have attached'. Enti, wɔ English a wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara no, wɔde 'would' ne 'could' sɛdeɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara, na wɔ Twi no, wɔde 'Podría' sɛdeɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara. Afeha biara: wɔ English no, wɔmmusɛ 'usted' anaa deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara no, noko wɔde kyerɛw a wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara ne deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara.
rule: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wode kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara a wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara no, ɛsɛ sɛ wode kyerɛw a wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara: 1) Deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara ne deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara: 'Dear Mr. Smith', 'Dear Madam', 'Yours sincerely', 'Yours faithfully'. 2) Deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara ne deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara: 'state' (na ɛnne 'say'), 'require' (na ɛnne 'need'), 'I would like to' (na ɛnne 'I want'), 'I am writing to inform you'. 3) Deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara: deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara, deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara, ne deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara. 4) Mmua deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara: de 'do not' na ɛnne 'don't', 'I would' na ɛnne 'I'd'. 5) Sɛ wode kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara: de deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara sɛ 'Introduction', 'Findings', 'Recommendations', ne deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara sɛ 'It was found that...' (Wɔhu sɛ...). 6) Deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara: 'Could you please...', 'I would appreciate...', 'Would it be possible to...?'. Fa so sɛ wɔ English a wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara no, wɔmmusɛ 'please' wɔ deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara no mu (ɛno ara na wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara), noko wɔde no wɔ deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara anaa deɛ wɔde kyerɛw wo dema ne mmara.

title: Dealing with Conflict / Kwantwom ne ahoɔden a edwuma
bridge: Wɔ Twiriso, yɛnkyɛ yɛbɛka adwuma a ɛyɛ den na yɛde 'ka wo ma me hu a ɛda ada' anaa 'sɛ yɛbɛyɛ' adi kan a wɔyɛ ahoɔden. Nanso, wɔ English, ɛsɛ sɛ yɛbɛyɛ adwuma a ɛyɛ den ne a yɛde kwan ma obi: yɛde mmara bɔfoɔ a wɔfrɛ no 'could' ne 'might', ne sɛ 'I feel...' na ɛnnyɛ sɛ yɛbɛka a wɔde ama yɛn. Sɛ yɛbɛka sɛ 'you must' a ɛne sɛ 'tienes que' a, ɛbɛyɛ den, na ɛsɛ sɛ yɛbɛka sɛ 'you might want to' anaa 'maybe you could'.
rule: Ma English a ɛyɛ B2, ɛsɛ sɛ yɛbɛka adwuma a ɛyɛ den ne a yɛde kwan ma obi. Nnipa a wɔyɛ adwuma no ne: 1) Mmara bɔfoɔ a wɔde ma obi adwuma a ɛyɛ den: 'could', 'might', 'would' (sɛ 'We could try...'). 2) Adwuma a yɛde yɛn ho adwene: 'I feel', 'I think', 'I believe' ma yɛnnhu sɛ yɛde ama obi. 3) Adwuma a ɛde ma yɛn adwuma: 'If you..., we could...'. 4) Adwuma a yɛde ma obi adwuma: 'I understand', 'I see your point'. 5) Adwuma a ɛde ma yɛn adwuma: 'I wonder if you could...'. 6) De 'sorry' ma obi adwuma a ɛnnyɛ sɛ yɛde ama obi: 'I'm sorry if that came across the wrong way'. Mma yɛnnhu sɛ yɛde 'you' ama obi adwuma (sɛ 'You are wrong') efisɛ ɛbɛyɛ den. Na yɛde 'I'm not sure that's accurate' anaa 'I see it differently'.

title: Summarising and Paraphrasing / Kɔbɔ ne Kɔbɔ ntɛm
bridge: Wɔ Twi, yɛnkyɛm yɛ kɔbɔ ntɛm ho asɛm de 'yɛn se', 'yɛn ka' ne 'kɔbɔ no mu', nanso wɔ English, discursive markers no wɔ hɔ paa ne wɔde wɔ kyerɛw no mu anaa asɛm no mu akɛse. Hwehwɛ: wɔ English no, wɔntumi de 'in summary' sɛnea wɔde 'in short' anaa 'to sum up' no da sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ, na wɔde verb 'summarize' no kyerɛw wɔ kyerɛw no ase. Ntɛm baako biara nso ɛha, sɛnea yɛde subject no kyerɛw paa wɔ Twi no, wɔ English no, pronoun ne ellipsis no ho nhyehyɛeɛ yɛ den, nanso subject no nni asɛm a ɛfiri ne ho nyinaa so.
rule: Ma wɔ B2 level no, wɔde verb sɛ 'summarize', 'paraphrase', 'outline', 'restate', ne connector phrases sɛ 'in other words', 'that is', 'to put it briefly', 'in a nutshell', 'to sum up', 'in short', 'all in all' ne 'to recap' no kɔbɔ ne kɔbɔ ntɛm. Structure a ɛsɛ sɛ wɔde no ɛyɛ: [Connector] + [clause a wɔde kɔbɔ asɛm no ho nhyehyɛeɛ no]. Sɛ wɔkɔbɔ ntɛm no, grammatical structure no susuw (sɛnea ɛbɛyɛ, active voice kɔ passive voice, anaa subordinate clause kɔ nominal phrase) nanso meaning no nyɛnko. Examples: 'The study reveals a significant increase...' → 'In other words, the numbers went up a lot.' Ma wɔkɔbɔ text bi no, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔbɔ 'The text is about...' anaa 'The author argues that...'. Sɛ wɔkɔbɔ no, ɛsɛ sɛ wɔnka 'en resumen' sɛ 'in summary' wɔ informal contexts no mu; de 'in short' anaa 'to sum up' nkutoo. Hwehwɛ nso sɛ wɔntumi de 'actually' (a ɛma 'en realidad', na ɛnni 'actualmente' ho asɛm) nanso wɔde 'in fact' anaa 'actually' ma wɔkɔbɔ no.

title: Using Idioms Naturally / Kasa nkyerɛkyerɛ a wɔde kasa ho asɛm
bridge: Wɔ Twi, mmoa nkyerɛkyerɛ no bɛyɛ paa na wɔde hɔn ama asɛm a wɔkasa no ho asɛm pɛ sɛ ‘wɔyɛ sɛ anantwi’ (‘estar como una cabra’). Wɔ English, mmoa nkyerɛkyerɛ pii wɔ hɔ a wɔde kyerɛw wɔ kasa a wɔkasa ho asɛm ne din a wɔde ama nnuan no, na wɔyɛ nkɔso na wɔato paa. Sɛde a wɔwɔ hɔ bi ara ne sɛ wɔbɔ mmoa nkyerɛkyerɛ a wɔde kasa ho asɛm no kyerɛw wɔ Twi so na wɔbɔ no wɔ English (sɛdeɛ ‘to have a good face’ na ɛnte sa ‘to be in a good mood’). Nso, English no de ‘to be’ ama asɛm pii sɛdeɛ ‘be over the moon’, na Twi no nso de ‘estar’ anaa ‘tener’. Fa akoma yie kyerɛw a wɔde kasa ho asɛm no: mmoa bi wɔ hɔ a wɔyɛ anigye (sɛdeɛ ‘kick the bucket’) na mmoa biara nso wɔ hɔ a wɔyɛ nnwim (sɛdeɛ ‘pass away’).
rule: Sɛ wopɛ sɛ wode mmoa nkyerɛkyerɛ a wɔde kasa ho asɛm no kyerɛw wɔ English, to nkyɛm nnɛm: 1. Sua mmoa nkyerɛkyerɛ no sɛdeɛ wɔwɔ hɔ, ɛnte sɛ wode kyerɛw wɔ tete a wode ama no. 2. Sua kyerɛw a wɔde kasa ho asɛm no: sɛ ɛyɛ formal, informal, colloquial anaa vulgar. Sɛdeɛ, ‘to be over the moon’ yɛ informal, nanso ‘to be delighted’ yɛ formal paa. 3. Mmoa nkyerɛkyerɛ pii wɔ hɔ a wɔn kyerɛw no yɛ nkyerɛkyerɛ, na ɛnte sɛdeɛ wɔde kyerɛw no. Sɛdeɛ, ‘break the ice’ ɛnte sɛ wɔde brɛɛ so ama nnuan, nanso ɛkyerɛ sɛ wɔde kyerɛw a wɔde ama nnuan a ɛyɛ anigye. 4. Wɔde mmoa nkyerɛkyerɛ no ama asɛm a wɔkasa no ho asɛm wɔ kɔmpɔnaa ne akwantu mu, nanso wɔntumi de no ama asɛm a wɔkasa no ho asɛm wɔ akwantu a ɛyɛ paa anaa a ɛyɛ soro. 5. Mmoa nkyerɛkyerɛ bi wɔ hɔ a wɔde ama nnuan wɔ mfonini biara (sɛdeɛ ‘to be in hot water’ wɔ American English mu na ‘to be in a pickle’ wɔ British English mu). 6. Deɛm ne deɛm a wɔde kasa no ho asɛm no yɛ pɛn: wɔde mmoa nkyerɛkyerɛ no kyerɛw sɛdeɛ wɔde kasa no ho asɛm, na wɔde contrations no ama asɛm a wɔkasa no ho asɛm wɔ kɔmpɔnaa mu (sɛdeɛ ‘it's raining cats and dogs’). 7. Mmoa nkyerɛkyerɛ nyinaa ɛnte sɛ wɔde ama asɛm a wɔkasa no ho asɛm; mmoa bi wɔ hɔ a wɔyɛ din anaa din a wɔde ama nnuan (sɛdeɛ ‘a piece of cake’ = something easy). 8. Sua tense a wɔde kasa no ho asɛm: mmoa nkyerɛkyerɛ pii wɔ hɔ a wɔde ama nnuan wɔ past tense mu (sɛdeɛ ‘he bit the bullet’), enti sua sɛdeɛ wode ama nnuan wɔ tense a ɛfata so.

common_error.wrong: I have a good face today.
common_error.correct: I'm in a good mood today.
common_error.explanation: Asɛm no adi sɛ wɔ Twi mu wɔde ‘tener buena cara’ anaa ‘tener buen semblante’. Sɛ wode kyerɛw wɔ tete a wode ama no, ɛbɛyɛ sɛ wɔde kyerɛw no ɛnte sa English. Wɔ English mu wɔde ‘to be in a good mood’ anaa ‘to be feeling good’. Mma wode mmoa nkyerɛkyerɛ a wɔde kasa ho asɛm no kyerɛw wɔ Twi so na wɔbɔ no wɔ English; sua mmoa a wɔde ama nnuan wɔ English mu.
